analysis:
Examined both threat-model excerpts, file metadata, the dependency pointer change, and the MediaIngest patch against the canonical definition index and selected details. MediaIngest.swift head lines 773–776 adds video/x-m4v and video/mov to an exact base64 data-URI allowlist; line 798 retains case-insensitive matching, and line 803 still passes the decoded-byte limit to dataFromDataURI. These aliases do not themselves admit file/http URLs or introduce disk writes. docs/threat-model.yaml lines 1967–1973 updates T-050 consistently with the aliases while retaining the stated container, external-reference and resource-limit contracts. The remaining supplied threat prose is unchanged according to the complete range map; historical limitations are not new findings.
No concrete regression is established in the visible provider patch. However, libs/mlx-swift-lm line 1 changes the dependency revision without supplying its implementation diff. This is a material coverage limit, not evidence of safety or a missing control. Integration must examine that revision delta, particularly MemoryBackedVideoAsset container sniffing, forbidAll reference restrictions, bounded resource-loader ranges, cancellation/ownership and frame processing consumed by MediaIngest. Confirm aliases still reach only the existing MP4/QuickTime memory-backed path and retain byte/duration/pixel/count/aggregate limits (T-050, A-001, TB-007). Any other upstream changes must also be checked for cache isolation/persistence (T-041), cancellation (T-010), output integrity (T-007) and memory exposure (T-028). No visible change here establishes altered authorization, attestation, transport encryption, token custody, billing or privileged fan controls; this local review does not validate their unchanged implementations.
